findings.claim: `_max_run_id` and `_attach_runs_minted_since` (line 71) reach past `Ledger`'s public surface into `ledger._db`, the private `sqlite3.Connection`, and hand-write SQL against the `runs` table's `run_id`/`batch_id` columns. Every other production module in the repo (session.py, scheduler.py, cli.py, reconcile.py, package.py) and every other line in this same file talks to the ledger exclusively through named methods (`create_batch`, `close_batch`, `attach_run_to_batch`, `batch_spend`); `batch.py` is the only non-`ledger.py` module that touches `_db` at all. This duplicates schema knowledge that is supposed to live solely in `ledger.py`, so a future change there (a column rename, a different run-id strategy, a non-SQLite backend) can silently break this sweep without anyone touching `batch.py`, and no gate here checks for it since `_db` is syntactically an ordinary attribute.

Same boundary violation as line 45: raw SQL against `runs.batch_id IS NULL` reimplements what should be a `Ledger` query method. The comment block above it argues carefully for the `run_id > high_water` scoping, which is exactly the kind of invariant that belongs behind a named, tested `Ledger` method (as `attach_run_to_batch` already is) rather than inlined SQL a caller outside `ledger.py` is trusted to get right.

No test checks that a run is attached to its batch when the outcome is an abort state (GATE_ERROR/PREFLIGHT_FAILED/RATE_LIMITED) rather than a state the task earned. Moving `ledger.attach_run_to_batch(outcome.run_id, batch_id)` from its current unconditional position into only the `else` branch (so it runs for earned states but not for aborts) keeps every test in test_batch.py green — the two abort tests (`test_two_consecutive_aborts_fire_the_breaker`, `test_an_exhausted_task_between_two_aborts_resets_the_breaker`) only assert on `runner.calls` and the returned reason, never on the `runs.batch_id` column — while silently breaking the acceptance criterion 'Each run the night produces is attached to the batch,' and specifically the runs whose cost the design notes say matters most: aborted tasks that still billed a preflight and a baseline suite before dying.
